Can we use slurry of human excreta instead of cowdung slurry to produce biogas in a typical biogas plant? Support your answer giving reasons.
rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: it also accepts "in human excreta methanogens are absent" as the reason. That is too strong: methanogens such as Methanobrevibacter also live in the human gut, and biogas plants fed with human excreta do exist. The sound reason is the NCERT one given below, that cattle dung is rich in methanogens.]

**No**, not in a typical biogas (gobar gas) plant. Reasons:
- Biogas is produced by **methanogens** such as **Methanobacterium**, which grow **anaerobically on cellulosic material** and produce large amounts of **methane** along with \(\text{CO}_2\) and \(\text{H}_2\).
- These bacteria are commonly found in the **rumen of cattle**, where they help break down the cellulose of the fodder, so **cattle dung (gobar) is rich in methanogens** and carries plenty of undigested cellulose for them to act on.
- A typical biogas plant is designed around cowdung slurry as this source of methanogens; human excreta is not a comparable source of them, so the plant would not yield biogas in the same way.

rows.stem: State the mode of action of cocain on human body. Write the scientific name of the source plant it is obtained from.
rows.solution:
Mode of action: cocaine **interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine**. As a result it has a **potent stimulating action on the central nervous system**, producing a sense of **euphoria and increased energy**. Excessive dosage causes **hallucinations**.

Source plant: cocaine is obtained from the coca plant, **Erythroxylum coca**, native to South America.

rows.stem: Write the best method to measure the population density of a single Banyan tree in comparison to 20 Parthenium weeds in a forest by an ecologist. Explain and justify your answer.
rows.solution:
For such a comparison the best measure of population density is **percent cover or biomass**, not the number of individuals.

Justification:
- Population density is normally measured as the number of individuals per unit area, but the number is not always the most meaningful measure.
- A **single huge Banyan tree** with a large canopy plays a far bigger role in the forest than **20 Parthenium weeds**, though by numbers the weeds would appear twenty times more abundant.
- The **canopy (percent cover) or biomass of the single Banyan tree is much more than that of the 20 Parthenium plants**, so measuring percent cover or biomass reflects the true size of each population in the area.

rows.stem:
(i) Write the observations made at the end of Connell's field experiment on barnacles on the rocky sea coasts of Scotland.
(ii) Name any two categories of organisms that in general are adversely affected by competition.
rows.solution:
(i) In Connell's elegant field experiments on the rocky sea coasts of Scotland, the **larger and competitively superior barnacle Balanus dominates the intertidal area**, and **excludes the smaller barnacle Chthamalus** from that zone. This is evidence of competitive exclusion in nature.

(ii) **Herbivores** and **plants** in general appear to be more adversely affected by competition than carnivores.

rows.subtopic: Species Numbers and Patterns of Biodiversity
rows.stem:
The graphs (X) and (Y) given below depict the diurnal variations in the solar radiations in the month of June (Summer) and in December (Winters) :
(i) Which of the two graphs depicts tropical region and temperate regions respectively ?
(ii) Which of the two regions (X) or (Y) will show high biological diversity and why?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED: four small graphs side by side, each of Solar radiation (y, arrow upward) against Time of the day (x, ticks 1 hr., 12, 24 hr.), each with one hump-shaped curve peaking at 12; the first two are captioned June 22 and Dec. 22 under the label (X), the last two June 22 and Dec. 22 under the label (Y). How tall each hump is, and so how much each region's radiation changes between June and December, is what part (i) asks the student to read, so it is withheld here. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
The marking scheme judged these graphs not conclusive enough for any interpretation and awards the mark for part (i) to every student who attempts it.

(i) The question is meant to be read by the **change between June and December**:
- In graph (Y) the June and December curves are of the **same height**: solar radiation hardly varies with the season, which is the mark of a **tropical region**.
- In graph (X) the June curve is much taller than the December one: radiation **varies strongly with the season**, which is the mark of a **temperate region**.

So the tropical and temperate regions are **(Y) and (X)** respectively. The graphs are inconclusive because the tallest curve of all is X's June curve, although a tropical region receives more solar energy over the year, which is why the board gave the mark for any attempt.

(ii) Region **(Y), the tropical region**, will show higher biological diversity, because (any one):
- tropical environments are **less seasonal**, relatively more **constant and predictable**, and such constant environments promote **niche specialisation**, leading to greater species diversity;
- **more solar energy** is available in the tropics, which contributes to higher productivity;
- tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years and so had a **long evolutionary time for species diversification**.

rows.stem: 'An HIV patient normally doesn't die of 'AIDS', but death is caused due to many other infections.' Do you agree with the statement ? Give explanatory reasons in support of your answer.
rows.solution:
**Yes**, I agree with the statement. Reasons:
- After getting into the body, HIV enters the **macrophages**, which act like an HIV factory, and the **helper T-lymphocytes (\(\text{T}_\text{H}\) cells)**, in which it replicates and produces progeny viruses.
- The progeny viruses attack other helper T-lymphocytes, so there is a **progressive decrease in the number of helper T-lymphocytes** in the infected person.
- As a result the person becomes **immuno-deficient**: the immune system is unable to protect the body against infections.
- The patient therefore becomes prone to infections by **Mycobacterium, viruses, fungi and even parasites like Toxoplasma**, which would otherwise have been overcome. These infections, and not the virus itself, are the usual cause of death.

rows.stem:
(a) Why do doctors have to carry many tests for selecting a person to be a suitable donor for someone who is going for an organ transplant and not take the organ from just anybody ? Explain giving reason.
(b) Name the drug a patient who has undergone a successful organ transplant, has to take all his/her life.
rows.solution:
(a) Doctors test many people to find a matching donor **to avoid graft rejection**.
- Grafts from just any source cannot be made; tissue matching and **blood group matching** are essential before undertaking any graft or transplant.
- The body's immune system is able to **differentiate between 'self' and 'non-self'**. An organ that does not match is recognised as foreign.
- The **cell-mediated immune response** of the T-lymphocytes then attacks it, and the graft is rejected.

(b) The patient has to take **immuno-suppressants** (immuno-suppressive drugs, such as **cyclosporin A**) all his or her life, to keep the immune system from rejecting the transplanted organ.

rows.subtopic: Isolation, Cutting and Amplification of DNA
rows.stem: A cell free method of amplifying DNA first developed in the mid 1980's revolutionized the field of biotechnology. Name the method and explain the basic steps of the technique involved.
rows.solution:
The method is the **Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)**, in which multiple copies of a gene (or DNA) of interest are synthesised in vitro.

Basic steps:
- **Denaturation**: the double-stranded DNA is **heated** so that its two strands separate.
- **Annealing**: two sets of **primers**, small chemically synthesised oligonucleotides complementary to the regions of DNA flanking the gene, **join (anneal) to the complementary regions** of the single strands.
- **Extension**: the **primers are extended** using the nucleotides provided in the reaction and the template DNA, by a **thermostable DNA polymerase** (**Taq polymerase**, isolated from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus), which remains active during the high temperature of denaturation.

The cycle is **repeated many times**, so the segment of DNA is **amplified** to approximately a billion times, that is, a billion copies are made.

rows.subtopic: Species Numbers and Patterns of Biodiversity
rows.stem:
Given below is an equation describing the Species-Area relationship between species richness and area for a wide variety of taxa as angiosperm plants, birds, bats etc.
\(S = CA^{Z}\)
(i) Give a graphical representation of the given equation showing Species-Area relationship.
(ii) What does 'S' represent in the given equation ?
(iii) What is the value of 'Z' (regression coefficient) for frugivorous birds and mammals in the tropical forests of different continents ?
rows.solution:
(i) The graph is drawn with **species richness (S)** on the y-axis against **area (A)** on the x-axis. Within a region, species richness increases with increasing explored area, but only up to a limit, so the curve **rises steeply and then levels off**: it is a **rectangular hyperbola**, labelled \(S = CA^{Z}\). On a logarithmic scale the same relationship is a **straight line**, \(\log S = \log C + Z \log A\).

(ii) **S** represents **species richness**. (In the equation A is the area, Z the slope of the line or regression coefficient, and C the Y-intercept.)

(iii) For frugivorous (fruit-eating) birds and mammals in the tropical forests of different continents, the slope **Z is found to be 1.15**. For small areas Z usually lies between 0.1 and 0.2, but over very large areas such as whole continents the line is much steeper.

rows.context: Cloning of genes, play a very significant role in genetic engineering, helping the transfer of desirable foreign genes into different hosts. The scientists, to make this process easier and effective are creating engineered vectors in such a way that they help easy linking of foreign DNA and selection of recombinants from non recombinants. 'pBR322' is one such engineered vectors developed by scientists. A diagram of an engineered vector pBR322 is given below :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED: a circular map labelled pBR322 in the centre, the ring divided into shaded segments, with printed labels Cla I and Hind III (top), Pvu I and Pst I (upper left), tet^R inside the ring (upper right) and Sal I (right), and six quoted letters 'U', 'V', 'W' (segments inside the ring) and 'X', 'Y', 'Z' (sites marked by leader lines outside it). Which letter marks which segment or site, and so which is rop and which is ori, is decided by the drawing and is withheld here. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
- **rop** is **'W'**. It **codes for the proteins involved in the replication of the plasmid**.
- **ori** is **'U'**. It is the **origin of replication**, the sequence from where replication starts; any piece of DNA linked to it can replicate within the host cells, and it is also responsible for **controlling the copy number** of the linked DNA.

rows.stem:
Draw the fragments that will be formed by the action of 'Z' (marked in the diagram) on the specific site of the DNA segment given below :
5' --- GTACGAATTCCTGA---3'
3'---CATGCTTAAGGACT---5'
rows.context: Cloning of genes, play a very significant role in genetic engineering, helping the transfer of desirable foreign genes into different hosts. The scientists, to make this process easier and effective are creating engineered vectors in such a way that they help easy linking of foreign DNA and selection of recombinants from non recombinants. 'pBR322' is one such engineered vectors developed by scientists. A diagram of an engineered vector pBR322 is given below :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED: the case study's pBR322 map, where the letter 'Z' is defined: a leader line from 'Z' to a restriction site on the ring. Which enzyme's site 'Z' marks decides where the given segment is cut, so its position on the ring is withheld here. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
'Z' marks the site of the restriction enzyme **EcoR I**, which recognises the palindromic sequence **5' GAATTC 3'** and cuts each strand **between G and A**. In the given segment this site is
5'---GTAC**GAATTC**CTGA---3'
3'---CATG**CTTAAG**GACT---5'

So the two fragments formed are:

Fragment 1:
5'---GTACG 3'
3'---CATGCTTAA 5'

Fragment 2:
5' AATTCCTGA---3'
3' GGACT---5'

Because the cut is a little away from the centre of the palindrome, each fragment carries a single-stranded **AATT overhang** at its 5' end. These overhangs are the **sticky ends**: they form hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts, which lets DNA ligase join DNA cut by the same enzyme.

rows.stem:
(i) How does the treatment with 2.5 mg/kg brings an effect on cholesterol metabolism when compared from 24 hours and 144 hours.
(ii) Write any two natural sources from where dsRNA molecule could be obtained for silencing the specific mRNA.
(iii) How is RNAi used in controlling the infection on the roots of tobacco plants by the nematode Meloidogyne incognitia.
rows.context:
RNA interference (RNAi) holds great potential as a therapeutic agent for the treatment of human diseases and as biocontrol agents in controlling pests in the field of agriculture. An experiment was carried to study the use of 'RNAi' for the potential treatment of disorders of cholesterol metabolism. Some people possess genetic mutations with elevated levels of ApoB gene which predisposes them to coronary artery diseases.

Lowering the amount of ApoB can reduce the number of lipoproteins and lower the blood cholesterol.

Tracy Zimmerman and her colleagues used RNAi in 2006 to reduce the level of ApoB in non human primates Cynomolgus monkeys.

One group of monkeys were given RNAi treatment (small interfering RNAs, SiRNAs) (doses 1 mg/kg SiRNAs), second group of monkeys were given RNAi treatment (doses 2.5 mg/kg SiRNAs) and third group of monkeys were injected with saline.

The results of the study are depicted in the graph below :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED: a bar graph of Relative serum cholesterol (% predose) (y, 0 to 120 in steps of 20) against Time (hours) at 24, 48, 144 and 264 (x), with three bars at each time keyed Saline - X (diagonal hatching), 1 mg/kg - Y (dotted outline) and 2.5 mg/kg - Z (solid grey). The bar heights, and so how the 2.5 mg/kg bar changes between 24 and 144 hours, are what part (i) asks the student to read, so they are withheld here. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
(i) The bar Z (2.5 mg/kg SiRNAs) falls from about 63 at 24 hours to about 43 at 144 hours, while the saline control X rises over the same period. So there is a **considerable decrease in the level of serum cholesterol after 144 hours as compared to 24 hours** of treatment with 2.5 mg/kg SiRNAs: the SiRNAs have silenced the ApoB gene, and the effect grows with time.

(ii) Natural sources of the complementary dsRNA:
- **infection by viruses having RNA genomes** (RNA viruses, retroviruses);
- **mobile genetic elements (transposons, jumping genes)** that replicate via an RNA intermediate.

(iii) RNAi is used to make tobacco plants resistant to the nematode Meloidogyne incognita, which infects their roots:
- Using **Agrobacterium vectors**, **nematode-specific genes** are introduced into the host (tobacco) plant.
- The introduced DNA is made to produce **both sense and anti-sense RNA** in the host cells.
- These two RNAs, being **complementary** to each other, form a **double-stranded RNA (dsRNA)**.
- The dsRNA **initiates RNAi** and thus **silences the specific mRNA of the nematode**.
- As a result the parasite **could not survive in the transgenic host** expressing the specific interfering RNA, and the transgenic plant is protected from the parasite.
